speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) whether he can provide an update on the number of HDB blocks that are not given lift upgrading due specifically to the funding cap; and (b) whether HDB will consider polling the residents in these affected blocks to explore the possibility of co-sharing the amount beyond the funding cap to have lift access at their floors.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Over the years, HDB has adopted innovative technical solutions to provide such blocks with lift access.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For some of the blocks where LUP is not feasible, the cost of providing 100% lift access would be prohibitive.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: LUP is done on a polling basis and, if the poll is successful, those who do not vote in favour of LUP still have to pay their share of the cost.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Singaporeans who are in urgent need of direct lift access due to medical conditions or disability may approach HDB for housing and financial assistance.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: HDB will assess each request on a case-by-case basis to see how best to render help.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For these remaining blocks, HDB continues to look at available technical and innovative solutions to see how we can provide for these blocks and, as and when they become available, we will make that option possible.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Those blocks that cannot get LUP because of the funding cap, why in the first place did the Ministry not put them under the main LUP contract because they will enjoy huge economies of scale when it comes to bidding?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: If I build one lift, it is more expensive, I do not mind throwing in a few other freebies.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: If the whole thing were to be parked under the original LUP, I think those blocks which have funding cap issues will probably be resolved.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I do not know whether the Ministry could consider throwing another tender for all these lifts.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some of the 150 blocks are not eligible for LUP because of very severe site constraints.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, even if you drive this as a part of the overall LUP, which they were, because, LUP, when you call the contract, it is for all unavailable blocks that qualify.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, that is a very different order altogether.
